profile.reading:
The address on file for this entry, 7400 North Lakewood Avenue in Tulsa's Cherokee Industrial Park, corresponds to a large, well-documented enterprise data center whose ownership history is publicly recorded, even though a direct link to the operator currently listed here, Experian, could not be independently confirmed in this research. Local business press reports the building was originally constructed in 2001 and developed for Electronic Data Systems (EDS), which operated it as a "Service Management Center" - trade coverage describes it as roughly 430,000 square feet, with about 80,000 square feet of raised-floor technical space capable of housing more than 12,000 servers, and notable for having much of its structure built partially underground, an unusual design choice reported as aimed at physical resilience. The facility underwent a capacity-doubling expansion in 2009, the same year Hewlett-Packard completed its acquisition of EDS, folding the Tulsa site into HP's enterprise-services division.

In July 2014, HP purchased the real estate outright for $150 million from BNP Paribas, which had held it under a sale-leaseback financing arrangement. Local officials at the time called it one of the largest real-estate-only transactions in Tulsa history, with the county's own assessed value on the property put at roughly $170.2 million. Coverage of the purchase described roughly 800 HP employees working at the site, supporting cloud storage and data services reported to include aviation-industry systems such as flight tracking, ticketing, reservations, and weather-data processing - consistent with the large, sticky enterprise IT-outsourcing contracts EDS and later HP Enterprise Services were known for.

HP's enterprise-services business was later spun off and merged into DXC Technology in 2017, and independent industry data-center listings identify DXC Technology, not Experian, as the current named operator of a large Tulsa, Oklahoma facility with published capacity around 20 megawatts, with HP Enterprise Services, LLC still recorded as the developing/owning entity - a chain of custody that lines up closely with the EDS-to-HP-to-DXC history above and with this address's Cherokee Industrial Park location.

Experian, a credit-reporting and data-analytics company, maintains business operations in Oklahoma, but no Experian-published source identified in this research names a Tulsa, Oklahoma data center, and the operator attribution for this specific registry record should be treated as unconfirmed pending a source that directly ties Experian, rather than the well-documented EDS/HP/DXC ownership chain, to this Cherokee Industrial Park building.

reading.body:
Cherokee Data Center in Tulsa has no published power specification, making it impossible to assess its scale relative to AI infrastructure needs. The facility is identified as a corporate data center operated by Experian at a specific address in the Cherokee Industrial Park, but Experian's own published materials do not disclose its power capacity, cooling, or IT load.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities, none with published megawatt figures from operator spec pages. Cherokee Data Center would rank first in the state by published capacity only because the state has published zero capacity figures across all sites, making the ranking meaningless for infrastructure analysis.

Without disclosed power specifications, rack density, or grid interconnection details, this facility cannot be evaluated for relevance to AI scaling. The absence of published figures is consistent across Oklahoma's mapped infrastructure and reflects either operator confidentiality for corporate facilities or incomplete disclosure to industry reference sources.
